texts.text: moving average ribbons (MARs) Wide bands of mathematically related and color-coded moving averages.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: narrow range bar (NR) A price bar with a smaller high-low range as compared to the prior bar's high-low range.
texts.text: narrow range bar (NR) A price bar with a smaller high-low range as compared to the prior bar's high-low range.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: narrowest  range  of  the  last  seven  bars  (NR7) A  low  volatility  timeprice convergence that often precedes a major price expansion. A price bar with a smaller high-low range as compared to the prior six bars' high-low ranges.
texts.text: narrowest  range  of  the  last  seven  bars  (NR7) A  low  volatility  timeprice convergence that often precedes a major price expansion. A price bar with a smaller high-low range as compared to the prior six bars' high-low ranges.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: NR7-2 The second NR7 in a row. A low volatility time-price convergence that often precedes a major price expansion.
texts.text: NR7-2 The second NR7 in a row. A low volatility time-price convergence that often precedes a major price expansion.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: neckline A trendline drawn under the support of a head and shoulders pattern over the resistance of an inverse head and shoulders pattern.
texts.text: neckline A trendline drawn under the support of a head and shoulders pattern over the resistance of an inverse head and shoulders pattern.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: negative feedback Directionless price action in which bars move back and forth between well-defined boundaries.
texts.text: negative feedback Directionless price action in which bars move back and forth between well-defined boundaries.

texts.text: On  Balance  Volume  (OBV) A  volume  indicator  that  measures  the progress of accumulation-distribution.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: opening  price  principle A  tendency  in  the  futures  markets  for  the opening price to act as support or resistance for the entire session.
texts.text: opening  price  principle A  tendency  in  the  futures  markets  for  the opening price to act as support or resistance for the entire session.

texts.text: oscillator A subset of technical indicators that accurately measures flat market conditions by assigning overbought and oversold price levels.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: overbought The evolution of price action to a state in which it runs out of buying pressure.
texts.text: overbought The evolution of price action to a state in which it runs out of buying pressure.

texts.label: text

texts.text: oversold The evolution of price action to a state in which it runs out of selling pressure.

texts.label: text

texts.text: pattern  analysis Price  prediction  through  interpretation  of  the  crowd behavior seen in repeating chart formations.

texts.text: pattern  cycles The  tendency  of  markets  to  repeat  identical  price  formations through different stages of development in all time frames. The master market blueprint that generates all chart patterns.

texts.text: pennants Small continuation patterns that print against the direction of the primary trend.

texts.text: %WIN A  performance  measurement  that  shows  the  total  number  of winners divided by the total number of trades.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: positive feedback Directional price action in which bars gather momentum and move from one level to the next.
texts.text: positive feedback Directional price action in which bars gather momentum and move from one level to the next.

texts.text: power  spike A  trading  strategy  that  seeks  high-volume  events  and executes positions to capitalize on their special characteristics.

texts.label: text

texts.text: profit target The projected price at which a successful trade will be terminated. The price at which a trade faces first resistance.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Random Walk Classic theory that chaos drives all market activity and that price movement cannot be predicted.
texts.text: Random Walk Classic theory that chaos drives all market activity and that price movement cannot be predicted.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: rectangle Small continuation pattern that prints sideways to the primary trend.
texts.text: rectangle Small continuation pattern that prints sideways to the primary trend.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: reflection A  two-four-bar  candlestick  pattern  that  first  prints  a  significant reversal and then thrusts away from that formation and immediately draws an identical reversal in the opposite direction.
texts.text: reflection A  two-four-bar  candlestick  pattern  that  first  prints  a  significant reversal and then thrusts away from that formation and immediately draws an identical reversal in the opposite direction.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Relative Strength Index A technical indicator that measures a stock's ability  to  close  up  rather  than  down  for  a  specific  period  of  time.  An oscillator invented by J. Welles Wilder that measures overbought, oversold, and divergent market situations.
texts.text: Relative Strength Index A technical indicator that measures a stock's ability  to  close  up  rather  than  down  for  a  specific  period  of  time.  An oscillator invented by J. Welles Wilder that measures overbought, oversold, and divergent market situations.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: ribbon crosspoint A horizontal support and resistance zone created by a moving average crossover.
texts.text: ribbon crosspoint A horizontal support and resistance zone created by a moving average crossover.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: rinse job An intraday shakeout in which price surges above resistance or below support, triggering the stops at those levels, and then changes direction, closing back within congestion. Similar to stop gunning .
texts.text: rinse job An intraday shakeout in which price surges above resistance or below support, triggering the stops at those levels, and then changes direction, closing back within congestion. Similar to stop gunning .

texts.text: rising wedge Reversal pattern that slowly rises in an uptrend until price suddenly ejects into a selloff.

texts.text: Santa rally The tendency of stocks to move higher in December, in a year-end event that marks up institutional portfolios.

texts.text: seasonality The predictable appearance of certain market characteristics that reflect specific and repeating calendar events.

texts.label: text

texts.text: shooting  star A  one-  to  three-bar  candlestick  reversal  pattern  with  a small real body and tall shadow that pushes into an intermediate high or low before a sudden change in direction.

texts.text: signpost Point  on  the  charting  landscape  that  identifies  an  imminent trading opportunity.

texts.text: silent alarm A rare high-volume signal that prints a narrow-range bar and flags an impending breakout.

texts.label: text

texts.text: 6-18 swing A moving average crossover system used to track intraday buying and selling pressure.

texts.label: text

texts.text: slippage The difference between expected transaction costs and actual transaction costs.

texts.label: text

texts.text: slippery slope Bollinger Band  pattern that indicates a sustained decline.

texts.orig: Stochastics An overbought-oversold oscillator that compares the current bar to a preset selection of high and low prices. The indicator plots the results on a graph between 0 and 100.

texts.text: stop  gunning An  intraday  shakeout  in  which  price  surges  above resistance or below support, triggering the stops at those levels, and then changes direction, closing back within congestion. Similar to a rinse job .

texts.label: text

texts.orig: Alan S.  Farley is  publisher  and  editor  of  HardRightEdge.com, an online trader's resource covering technical analysis, short-term trading tactics, and more. A professional trader with more than 20 years of experience, Farley has been a senior contributor for TheStreet.com for nearly a decade and  has  been  featured  in Barron's,  SmartMoney, Tech  Week,  Fidelity  Outlook, Schwab's On Investing, Forbes, Technical Analysis of Stocks and Commodities, Futures Magazine,  Active Trader,  MSN  Money, Technical  Investor,  Bridge Trader,  Online Investor, Los Angeles Times, and Trading Markets. He lives in Phoenix, Arizona.
